newsitem.title: IRAN: Iranian parliament to create women commission.
newsitem.headline: Iranian parliament to create women commission.

text.p: Iran's parliament has approved the outline of a bill to create a special commission to focus on women's issues and family affairs, newspapers said on Thursday.
Out of 195 deputies, 136 voted on Wednesday to approve the bill against opposition by conservatives who had undermined attempts to create the commission in 1992 and 1993.

The bill marked the first time that parliament approved the establishment of a commission on women. It is expected to undergo further approvals, but it was not immediately clear how the commission would work.
Since Iran's 1979 revolution, the country's conservative rulers have imposed a strict code of behaviour on women and stripped many of their freedoms.
Monireh Nobakht, one of ten female deputies, said: "We need a special body in the legislature to focus and address the problems of women."
Abbas Abbasi, an opponent of the bill, told Resalat newspaper: "What is so special about women? Why not create other commissions for men, children or old men as well?"

Defenders of the bill argued that as Iranian leaders encouraged 32 million Iranian women to take up social and political responsibilities there was a need for "coordination and re-definition of women's rights."
